entities.summary: A complete high-pass crossing beneath Blüemlisalp ice, climbing the dramatic Hohtürli stair system before descending to Oeschinensee and Kandersteg.
entities.description: Griesalp → Bundalp → Hohtürli → optional Blüemlisalphütte → Oberbärgli → Oeschinensee → Kandersteg. Red-white-red mountain trail with SAC T3 sections; moderate exposure on very steep stairs and loose high-pass terrain. Best July–September after snowmelt. No route-specific closure was found on 2026-08-11, but hard/fresh snow, wind and thunderstorms can make the upper pass unsuitable.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The pass, glacier scenery and Oeschinensee finale form a much stronger destination hike than treating the lake as a standalone outing.

names.canonical: Three classic passes — Grimsel, Furka & Susten

entities.summary: A 131 km Swiss alpine loop from Meiringen linking the Grimsel, Furka and Susten passes in one continuous high-mountain circuit.
entities.description: Starting and finishing in Meiringen, the loop crosses the Grimsel to Gletsch, climbs the Furka toward Andermatt, continues through Wassen to the Susten, and returns via Innertkirchen. Switzerland Tourism lists a May-to-October season and advises checking local route and weather conditions because high-pass access can be interrupted by seasonal or weather closures.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The route combines three major Swiss passes into one coherent circuit, moving through lake-and-waterfall country, glacier-facing high alpine terrain and long engineered mountain-road descents without requiring three separate out-and-back detours.

entities.summary: A steep historic path above Foroglio into a hanging side valley of waterfalls, stone bridges, boulder shelters and preserved seasonal settlements.
entities.description: Foroglio → waterfall-side historic path → Puntid → Gerra → Calnègia → return. Red-white-red mountain trail; about T2; low exposure, but old stonework becomes slippery when wet. Best May–October; avoid intense rain. No route-specific closure was found in the official 2026 route source.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Most visitors stop at Foroglio waterfall; continuing into Calnègia reveals the exceptional human-landscape adaptation that makes Val Bavona destination-worthy.

entities.summary: A point-to-point crossing through the Breccaschlund karst cirque and old pasture landscape before crossing toward Jaun.
entities.description: Schwarzsee / Gypsera → Brecca → Euschels → Jaun. Red-white-red mountain trail; about T2; low exposure. Best June–October. No route-specific closure was found in the 2026 research.

entities.summary: A quiet traverse through exceptionally high-elevation Swiss stone-pine forest and a cultural mountain pass between S-charl and Lü.
entities.description: S-charl → God da Tamangur → Alp Astras → Pass da Costainas → Lü. Red-white-red mountain trail; about T2; low exposure. Best July–October, especially autumn colour. No route-specific closure was found; seasonal bus schedules at both ends should be checked.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Forest atmosphere and cultural landscape give it substantial discovery value, particularly in autumn, even though it lacks the raw spectacle of the higher tiers.

entities.summary: A full Alpstein traverse from Hoher Kasten past Staubern and the Kreuzberge/Saxer Lücke walls, then down by Fählensee and Sämtisersee to Brülisau.
entities.description: Hoher Kasten → Staubern → Saxer Lücke → Bollenwees/Fählensee → Sämtisersee → Brülisau. Red-white-red mountain trail; about T2; low to moderate exposure and a very long descent. Best June–October. Hoher Kasten transport was operating in its 2026 summer season when checked; exact last service and trail conditions remain date-specific.
entities.whyWorthwhile: It turns the famous Saxer Lücke rock wall into a complete landscape journey, though the long descent and overlap with other Alpstein scenery keep it below A tier.
